findings.reason: The protected SQL solution selects seller.seller_name from Seller AS seller WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Orders AS orders WHERE orders.seller_id = seller.seller_id AND orders.sale_date BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31') ORDER BY seller.seller_name. The anti-join structure is concise, optimal, and handles sellers with no orders correctly; no candidate is required.

NOT EXISTS checks that no matching row exists in Orders for that seller with sale_date between 2020-01-01 and 2020-12-31. Sellers with orders outside 2020 or no orders at all fail the subquery condition and are correctly included.

Scanning s sellers against index-supported 2020 order lookups or hash anti-joins takes O((s + r) log(s + r)) time overall, and sorting the qualifying names takes O(s log s) time. Working space is O(s + r). Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Outputs single column seller_name, includes boundary dates 2020-01-01 and 2020-12-31, and sorts results by seller_name ASC.

The approach accurately details filtering 2020 sales, anti-joining Seller against Orders, preserving orderless sellers, and sorting by seller_name. Alternatives and edge cases cover correlated NOT EXISTS, NOT IN NULL traps, filtering all order history errors, boundary date inclusions, orderless sellers, multiple sales per seller, and sorting key correctness.
